prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D geometry of a small walled yard as the camera wearer looks forward at a perimeter wall and arched porch (roughly 2 to 4 m away in frame 1) before pitching their head steeply downward toward the ground (1 to 2 m below eye level) and turning left across frames 2 to 5. A standing person in a blue shirt is rendered as a bright foreground silhouette about 1.2 to 1.8 m in front of the camera wearer—shifting from the lower-left edge in frame 1 to the upper-left in frames 2 and 3, upper-right in frame 4, and far right in frame 5—while the wearer's own torso, legs, and gloved hands appear brightest at the bottom edge at 0.3 to 1.0 m. Throughout the sequence, the standing person faces away from the camera wearer toward the wall and bushes within their own arm's reach (about 0.5 m ahead of them) and never looks back, staying just at or slightly beyond the camera wearer's extended reach. Compared to RGB alone, the depth gradient clearly separates the standing person and protruding foliage from the flat ground plane and receding corner walls, while confirming the continuous distance between the wearer's lower body and the other person's feet. However, the map is unreliable where it assigns overly dark (far) values to the upper ground plane and shaded corners in frames 2 to 5, making continuous grass and wall surfaces appear as deep voids behind the standing figure.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the people in the yard against a black background, tracking the standing person (pink mask) about 1.2 to 1.8 m in front of the camera wearer and the camera wearer's own visible lower body and gloved hands (brown and cyan masks) at 0.3 to 1.0 m along the bottom edge in frames 2 to 5. As the camera wearer tilts their head down and rotates left across the five frames, the standing person's mask moves from being heavily cropped at the bottom-left border in frame 1 to fully visible from behind in the upper-middle field in frames 2 to 4, and then partially cropped at the right border in frame 5. The contour of the pink mask shows the standing person oriented away from the camera wearer toward the unsegmented bushes and wall, while the wearer's own hands in frames 3 and 4 remain near their waist, roughly 1.0 to 1.2 m away from the other person. This map makes it easy to distinguish the exact pixel boundaries of the camera wearer's self-occluding body parts from the other person and the cluttered vegetation in the RGB image. However, the segmentation is unreliable because it fragments the camera wearer's single body into multiple separate "person" instances (splitting torso, legs, and gloved hands in frames 3 and 4), misses the wearer's legs in frame 1, and omits all environmental structures such as walls, plants, and ground.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D body keypoints on a black background, detecting the standing person's torso and leg skeleton only in frames 3 and 4 at roughly 1.2 to 1.8 m in front of the camera wearer. In those two frames, the yellow shoulder-to-hip trapezoid and leg segments show the person standing upright below the top edge of the view, shifting from the upper-left in frame 3 to the upper-right in frame 4 as the camera wearer turns left. A tight cluster of facial/head keypoints sits just above the shoulder line while the arms are occluded in front of the torso, confirming that the person's back is turned to the camera wearer and they are looking away toward the wall and bushes within their own arm's reach. Compared to RGB, the wireframe makes the orientation of the torso, hip alignment, and knee/ankle joints explicit despite loose clothing and steep downward viewing angles. However, the map is highly unreliable across the strip: it completely fails to detect the standing person in frames 1, 2, and 5 when they are near the image borders or partially cropped, omits their right lower leg in frame 3, and never detects the camera wearer's own visible legs or gloved hands at the bottom of the frame.
